name: Aider
disclaimer: Written from documented interface, not verified against an install.
note: Unusual and useful: Aider keeps a human-readable transcript in the repo, so observation needs no vendor store.

file.note: Verified from the options reference (aider.chat/docs/config/options.html), read 2026-09-17: --message-file names a file containing the message to send the LLM, process the reply and exit, as --message does with the message itself.
As send: both are options of every aider command.

options.trust_none_why: aider works by editing files; it has no mode without its edit tools
options.unattended_note: Nothing is appended: resume already carries --yes-always.

--yes-always.why: Kept in every command because it is narrower than leaving it out. aider has no permission rules: --yes-always answers yes to its edit and file confirmations and no to running a shell command the model suggests (aider/io.py answers n to a question that needs an explicit yes), while a run without it takes each question's default from a closed stdin, yes to shell commands included. Read on 2026-09-17 from aider.chat/docs/config/options.html and github.com/Aider-AI/aider (aider/io.py).
